explainedBy: The host is holding a metal Slinky gripped from the top in his hand.

storyboard.claim: The host holds a metal Slinky gripped from the top.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The Slinky icon (a hand holding the coil from the top) beside the everyman.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Opening image.
storyboard.addedInformation: Establishes the object the whole episode returns to.

explainedBy: The same Slinky, heavy and tightly wound, gripped a few coils down.

storyboard.claim: The Slinky is heavy and tightly wound, gripped three or four coils down.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Same Slinky stage; the everyman now points at the coil.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same stage; action idle -> point at the coil.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: the grip position is carried by the audio.

explainedBy: Released, the bottom drops, catches itself and bounces down and up.

storyboard.claim: The bottom half drops and the Slinky bounces down and up.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The Slinky icon bounces; the everyman watches surprised.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same stage; face neutral -> surprised as the coil drops and bounces.
storyboard.addedInformation: The icon's own bounce shows the yo-yo motion.

explainedBy: The Slinky hangs suspended, bouncing rhythmically from the fingers.

storyboard.claim: The Slinky is suspended in a rhythmic bouncing dance.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Same Slinky, still bouncing; the everyman relaxes, pleased.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same stage; surprised -> happy, the bounce settles into rhythm.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: repeats the bounce; sets up the question.

explainedBy: The question: what caused the bounce of this Slinky, the hand or the spring?

storyboard.claim: What made the Slinky bounce - the hand that released it?
storyboard.concreteVisual: Same Slinky; the everyman asks, surprised.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same stage; the action becomes asking the question.
storyboard.addedInformation: Frames the cause question on the object itself.

explainedBy: Hand or spring? Our instinct points at the hand as the cause.

storyboard.claim: Hand or spring? Our brains are hardwired to point at the hand.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The everyman points at the hand holding the Slinky.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same stage; talk -> point, the intuitive answer.
storyboard.addedInformation: The pointing gesture is the intuition itself.

explainedBy: The intuitive linear chain: hand pulled away -> bottom dropped -> bounce.

storyboard.claim: Intuition says: simple linear cause and effect, the hand caused the bounce.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A three-step flow diagram of the hand-caused bounce.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the gesture to the chain it assumes.
storyboard.addedInformation: Makes the linear model explicit before it is refuted.

explainedBy: The host now holds the Slinky's cardboard box exactly the same way.
noVisual: No cardboard-box prop exists; the gift box is the closest held box, so the callout names it as the cardboard box.

storyboard.claim: Hold the Slinky's cardboard box the same way.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The everyman holding a box.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: A new object replaces the Slinky.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the swap of the object, same grip.

explainedBy: Same dramatic release, but the box just drops: nothing happens.

storyboard.claim: Same flourish, the bottom hand pulls away: nothing happens.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Same everyman with the box; face turns surprised.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same stage; neutral -> surprised.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: the drop itself is carried by the callout.

explainedBy: The box hits the floor with zero bounce, so the bounce was never in the hand.
noVisual: No falling-object animation; the now-empty hand and the callout carry the drop.

storyboard.claim: The box falls with zero bounce; the bounce was never in the hand.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The everyman's hand is now empty, his face blank.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same stage; the box is gone from his hand (hold -> idle).
storyboard.addedInformation: The empty hand shows the box fell and nothing came back.

explainedBy: Back to the Slinky: the bounce lives inside its own structure; the hand only released it.

storyboard.claim: The bounce was latent in the Slinky's structure; the hand just provided the release.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The Slinky returns and the everyman points at the coil itself.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same stage; the Slinky comes back, he points at the coil, not the hand.
storyboard.addedInformation: Contrast with the box: the coil holds the bounce.

callout.text: The central thesis of her framework

explainedBy: This image is the central thesis of Donella Meadows' framework.

storyboard.claim: That image is the central thesis of Meadows' framework.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Donella Meadows holding her book in a lecture room.
storyboard.onScreenText: The central thesis of her framework
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the demo to the author whose thesis it is.
storyboard.addedInformation: Introduces the author on screen.

explainedBy: Meadows lays out the premise of the deep dive.

storyboard.claim: The premise of the whole deep dive.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Same Meadows stage, now explaining.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same stage; hold -> talk.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: transition beat.

explainedBy: The stubborn problems that refuse to stay fixed: traffic, debt, burnout, collapsing oceans.

storyboard.claim: The most stubborn problems: gridlock traffic, personal debt, burnout, ocean ecosystem collapse.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A sorter of the four named problems.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the premise to its examples.
storyboard.addedInformation: Lists the four examples the narration names.

explainedBy: The hosts reject the usual explanation that people are stupid or evil.

storyboard.claim: These problems do not persist because people are stupid or evil.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The host speaking while the phrase is struck out.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the problems to the rejected explanation.
storyboard.addedInformation: The strike shows the rejection.

explainedBy: We keep turning the number dial instead of looking at the structure.

storyboard.claim: They persist because we keep pushing on the numbers instead of the structure.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The everyman reaching for a control dial.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the wrong explanation to the real one.
storyboard.addedInformation: The dial is the number we keep adjusting.

explainedBy: The giant lever that actually changes the system is the one we avoid touching.

storyboard.claim: The levers that work are the ones we want to avoid touching.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The everyman standing back, worried, from a giant iron lever.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Dial -> big lever; he stops reaching.
storyboard.addedInformation: Contrast: small dial touched, big lever avoided.

explainedBy: Facing the big lever is deeply unsettling; we must give something up.

storyboard.claim: It is deeply unsettling and requires giving something up.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Same lever; the everyman slumps.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same stage; idle -> slump.
storyboard.addedInformation: The slump shows the discomfort before the lever.

explainedBy: We love pointing a finger at a villain, like blaming political leaders.

storyboard.claim: We love the blame-the-villain game: pointing a finger at political leaders.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The everyman angrily pointing at a politician.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From discomfort to the habit we must surrender.
storyboard.addedInformation: Two-person blame relation made visible.

explainedBy: We cannot just blame the flu: our own exhaustion and lack of sleep set up the illness.

storyboard.claim: We can't just blame the virus; we set up the conditions - exhaustion, lack of sleep.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The everyman lying ill in bed.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Another blame target, now the body.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the sick, worn-out body the narration describes.

explainedBy: Whatever we blame, the Slinky bounces regardless of whose hand drops it.

storyboard.claim: Not competitors either: the Slinky bounces regardless of whose hand drops it.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The Slinky icon alone.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Back to the Slinky image to close the blame argument.
storyboard.addedInformation: Ties all the blame examples to the structure image.

callout.text: The behavior is in the structure

explainedBy: The mantra: the bounce (behavior) lives in the Slinky (structure).

storyboard.claim: The mantra: the behavior is in the structure.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Same Slinky icon, the mantra boxed.
storyboard.onScreenText: The behavior is in the structure
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same stage; the callout becomes the boxed mantra.
storyboard.addedInformation: The boxed label names the episode's thesis on its image.

explainedBy: Donella Meadows opens her book to define what a system is in her terms.

storyboard.claim: To grasp it we must define a system in Meadows' terms.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Donella Meadows opens her book to define what a system is in her terms.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From mantra to definition. (fix round 1: bare figure -> named object/diagram)
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: transition beat.

explainedBy: The three parts of any system, sorted: elements, interconnections, purpose.

storyboard.claim: Every system has three parts; first, the elements.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The three parts of any system, sorted: elements, interconnections, purpose.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same stage; talk -> point. (fix round 1: bare figure -> named object/diagram)
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: the parts are shown on the next beats.

explainedBy: Elements are visible physical things, like the trees in a forest.

storyboard.claim: Elements: the visible things, like trees in a forest or cars on a highway.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A tree in the forest set.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the list to its first part.
storyboard.addedInformation: The tree is a literal element example from the narration.

explainedBy: Interconnections are flows, like water moving through pipes.

storyboard.claim: Second, interconnections: physical flows like water through pipes, roads between cities.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A water icon.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From elements to how they relate.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the flow example.

explainedBy: Interconnections can be information signals, like a memo passing from a CEO down the company.

storyboard.claim: Or information signals: a memo from a CEO to a manager, a price signal.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The CEO holding a memo out toward a staff member.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From physical flows to information flows.
storyboard.addedInformation: The held memo between two people shows a signal passing.

explainedBy: The three parts of a system side by side: elements, interconnections, purpose.

storyboard.claim: Elements, interconnections, and third, purpose.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A three-bucket sorter of the system's parts.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Collects the parts named so far plus the third.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the full structure of a system at once.

explainedBy: A system's purpose is never written down; you deduce it by watching what it does.

storyboard.claim: Purpose is invisible; you deduce it by watching behavior over time.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The everyman examining with a magnifier.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the list to the hardest part, purpose.
storyboard.addedInformation: The magnifier shows deducing by observation.

explainedBy: Meadows' analogy: a frog turning left, right, backward, each time catching a fly.

storyboard.claim: A frog turns left, right, backward, and catches a fly each time.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The frog catching a fly with its tongue.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the abstract rule to the analogy.
storyboard.addedInformation: The icon shows the frog catching the fly.

callout.text: The purpose of the frog is turning

explainedBy: A viewer watches the frog turn and the narrator rejects the guess that turning is its purpose.

storyboard.claim: You don't conclude its purpose is turning.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Same frog; the wrong conclusion struck out.
storyboard.onScreenText: The purpose of the frog is turning
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same stage; adds the rejected reading.
storyboard.addedInformation: The strike marks the wrong inference.

explainedBy: Same watcher: the frog catching the fly shows the real purpose is catching flies.

storyboard.claim: Its purpose is catching flies: behavior reveals purpose.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Same frog catching the fly; the true purpose labelled.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same stage; the struck reading is replaced by the real purpose.
storyboard.addedInformation: The icon itself already shows the fly being caught.

explainedBy: The politician reads the speech: 'Our top priority' — words at the podium, not the budget.

storyboard.claim: A government says its top priority is protecting the environment.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The politician reads the speech: 'Our top priority' — words at the podium, not the budget.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the frog to human institutions. (fix round 1: bare figure -> named object/diagram)
storyboard.addedInformation: The smirk signals the speech is not to be taken at face value.

explainedBy: The budget gives that priority zero dollars and zero enforcement, so it is not the system's purpose.

storyboard.claim: The budget allocates zero dollars and zero enforcement: it is not the purpose.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Same politician now holding the wallet closed.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same stage; talk -> holding the wallet.
storyboard.addedInformation: The kept wallet contrasts with the spoken priority.

explainedBy: What the press release says, or what politicians believe, does not decide the purpose.

storyboard.claim: Regardless of the PR or what politicians believe.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Same politician talking, face blank; the PR is struck.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same stage; smirk -> blank, wallet put away.
storyboard.addedInformation: The strike marks the PR as dismissed.

explainedBy: Underfunding schools to fund corporate tax breaks reveals the purpose: wealth concentration.

storyboard.claim: If the system underfunds schools for tax breaks, its purpose is wealth concentration.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A flow diagram of the narrated chain.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the speech to what the system actually does.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the behavior-to-purpose chain.

explainedBy: Invisible forces pulling the strings that dictate our daily lives.

storyboard.claim: How do these invisible forces dictate our daily lives?
storyboard.concreteVisual: Invisible forces pulling the strings that dictate our daily lives.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From purpose to the mechanics of structure. (fix round 1: bare figure -> named object/diagram)
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: transition beat.

explainedBy: It starts with something basic but widely misunderstood.

storyboard.claim: It starts with something basic but misunderstood.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Same host, now eager.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same stage; neutral -> happy.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: transition beat.

explainedBy: The everyman sits by a filling bathtub as the warm water rises.

storyboard.claim: You sit in a bath; warm water slowly rises around your waist.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The everyman sitting beside the filling bathtub, relaxed.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: New example: the bath.
storyboard.addedInformation: The filling tub shows the rising water.

explainedBy: His hand rests on the faucet as water pours into the tub.

storyboard.claim: Hand on the cold faucet, feeling the water pour in.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Same tub; the everyman reaches to the faucet.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same stage; sit -> reach for the faucet.
storyboard.addedInformation: The reach puts his hand on the inflow.
